  `set_thread_state_act` sets `choose_new_thread` when ct is not `schedulable` (runnable ∧ bound to an active SC ∧ not
  released). ct is `Restart` after `schedule` in reachable states (e.g. a restarted thread chosen from a ready queue). l4v gets
  schedulability there from `valid_sched` (`valid_ready_qs` / `valid_sched_action`: active SC, not in the release queue).

  at the body's start σ0, factors as **`KP σ0 s := cfS s = cfS σ0 ∧ A8.CW σ0.curSc σ0 s ∧ RS σ0 s`** with **`RS σ0 s := resume s →
  sv (s.kheap ct0) = sv (σ0.kheap ct0) ∧ sv (s.kheap c0) = sv (σ0.kheap c0)`** (ct0 / c0 = σ0's ct / cur_sc, `SVK.sv` = rd's scheduler
  view) plus CtR at the end. OS by `os_frame` (cfS + CW); HRC / RCA because under resume ct0's and c0's views are σ0's (ct0 bound
  to c0 by CurScT, c0 active by CAx); CtR per arm: ct unbound or bound to cur_sc (`ctR_kp`: OffReady by `offReady_kp`), ct not
  runnable (`ctR_nrun`), or (receive_ipc's donated sender SC, not done) `RT` at the end.
  Every writer of ct's binding / cur_sc's TCB in handle_recv's cone reschedules first or is guarded off cur_sc: maybe_return_sc of ct
  (`when (tcbPtr = ct) reschedule_required`), the donation of ct's SC in send_fault_ipc (from = ct ⇒ test_reschedule), every
  refill_unblock_check (`scp ≠ cur_sc` tests), maybe_donate_sc of a bound thread (reads only).

  resume-view clause), `cw_of_cp` (CW from any rd8a CP lemma), **`ik_kp`** (any `SVM ∧ CFK` step), `kp_leaf` / `kp_auto` (rd8a's
  `cp_leaf` shape), hand leaves `kp_possibleSwitchTo` (heap kept: RdS's `ktc_possibleSwitchTo`), `sv_cancelIpc` (= rd8e's
  `sv_cancelIpc'`, duplicated here since rd8e is not on this base; drop one at merge) / `kp_cancelIpc`, `cfk_maybeReturnSc`,
  **`kp_maybeReturnSc n σ0`** (thread = σ0.curThread; the branch that unbinds ends with `rescheduleRequired_cn`); the end:
  **`offReady_kp`**, `kp_bind`, **`ss4_of_kp (BS σ0) (Suff σ0) (KP σ0 s) (CtR s) : SS4 s`**, **`ctR_kp`**, `ctR_nrun`.

## g2a (branch par/g2a in FL4-sc, on 063b674c = int/j2 incl. g3e, g3d, rd8a, ctq14) — G2 first step: `JAtZ.ext : JExt` (field `nat`, the native scope); `JDelParts.vt` and `KFinAtR27.vt` proved; `kernel_entryJ31` (DONE); `thr.obj`, `live`: NOT done (handoff)
Goal (INV-PLAN §4 G2, g3e (2) / g3d (B)): carry the joint extension as ONE sub-structure of `JAtZ` and turn the ∀-JAtZ
premises inside the top's bundles into theorems of it. Resumed once (predecessor cut off mid cone build; builds b1-b12 its, r2 mine).

### (1) `JExt` (JointAt.lean)
- `structure JExt th s : Prop` with ONE field so far: `nat : Vs.VsNat th (L.mem s)` [S] (G2 `nativeScopeX`; l4v: x64 has no VT-x
  objects): every slot's cap is `Vs.NativeCap` (VsFoot: no `Vcpu`, no `Ept`, no `Frame` with mapped ∧ EPT flag, no `IoPort` with
  owner ≠ 0). `JAtZ.ext : JExt Z.th s`; `JAtZR` / `JAtZS` carry it (`ext := J.ext`).
- Frame lemmas (the brief's `JExt.frame`): `JExt.of_eq` (caps of every slot kept), `JExt.ss` (`SlotsSame`), `JExt.step`
  (`Vs.VsSlotsT`, whose third conjunct is now `VsNat m → VsNat m'`), `Vs.VsNat.retype` (XTopJointUtEp: a retype's `RetExp`, old caps
  kept or untyped, new caps `Vs.nativeCap_newCapOf`).
- `Vs.MdbLike` gained a fourth part `vtF c' = vtF c` (`Vs.vtF`, `nativeCap_iff : NativeCap c ↔ vtF c = false`), so every remap
  (`VsLike`) keeps nativeness (`NativeCap.of_vtF`). Copies / mints / derives: `CnodeKey.copied_nat`, `MdbStepOps.mask_nat`,
  `update_nat`, `derive_nat`. IO-port control issue: the new cap has owner 0.
- 78 cone modules edited, each producer site adding ONE component (`J.ext.step hvT`, `J.ext.of_eq …`, `J.ext.ss hSS`,
  `⟨J.ext.nat.retype …⟩`, or an extra `VsSlotsT.of_some` argument `hn`). No new premise anywhere in the cone: every native FL4
  step (deletion loop WJL / WJLSwap / WJLFin / WJLEmpty, retype / reset of every object family, VSpace map / unmap / pool,
  CNode copy / mint / move / rotate / delete, TCB control / install, IRQ / IO control, IPC grant transfer, fault / reply,
  scheduler frames) keeps `JExt` already in this commit.

### (2) What became theorems
- `JVtHyps.ofExt` (XTopJointFinVtJ): `JVtHyps arI AR th` with NO premise. `io` / `ept` now ask for a non-native cap in a slot
  (they are read only at an owned IO-port / EPT / EPT-mapped frame finalisation, `JAtZ.frVtJ` / `finEptJ`, which pass that
  slot); `eptFr` / `vcpu` name an EPT-mapped Frame / Vcpu cap. All four refuted by `J.ext.nat`. So the brief's `vtIoPlace`
  field is NOT needed (its only reader is an owned IO-port cap's finalisation, ruled out by `nat`).
- `vtAsid_ofR` (XTopJointKEntry31): `KFinAtR27.vt` (∀-JAtZR vtable ASID, INV-PLAN F2) from the EXISTING `JAtZR.vsc`
  (`VCapOK`'s `.Pml4` clause: a mapped PML4 cap's ASID ≠ 0) and `JAtZR.jpl` / `zH` (a set TCB is the typed heap's). No JExt
  field needed (brief's (b) `vtAsid`).
- `kernel_entryJ31` (XTopJointKEntry31) = `kernel_entryJ30` with `hK : … → KDispHypsKV31` (`JEntryGlobM31.delParts :
  JDelPartsN` = `JDelParts` without `vt`) and `hFin : … → KFinAtR31` (= `KFinAtR27` without `vt`); wrappers `JDelPartsN.toJ`,
  `JEntryGlobM31.toM`, `KDispHypsKV31.to27b`, `KFinAtR31.to27`. No premise added; J30 kept.

### (3) Remaining premises touched by G2 (not done)
- `JDelPartsN.thr.obj` [S] (XTopJointDelR `JThreadFinHypsU.obj`, ∀-JAtZ: a Thread cap's TCB has VCPU word `p+3664 = 0`): still
  assumed. Not derivable from anything JAtZ carries: P1 (QueueVcpu docstring) says the TCB's VCPU word is a plain field no P1
  invariant reads (`plainW_all`). Needs a JExt field `vw : ∀ x p, IsSlot th x → capV m x = .Thread p → m (p+3664) = 0` with keep
  lemmas for every step that writes memory (not only caps): `JExt.of_eq` / `step` / `ss` would need the TCB word kept too, so
  every producer site needs a TCB-word frame (most steps' P1 footprints `WritesIn` give it; TCB retype zeroes it, `UtTcbInit`;
  only VCPU bind writes it, which is VT-x). Plan: add `vw` with `JExt.of_eq'` taking `hw : ∀ t, … m' (t+3664) = m (t+3664)`, and
  derive `hw` from the step's footprint at each site.
  Sizing (measured after 023cd448): the JExt uses funnel through generic rebuilds (38 explicit `J.ext.*` uses in 27 files), but
  their callers differ in what they know of FL4 memory: `JAtZ.sc_frame` (ScJointFrame; callers in 92 files) has
  `WritesIn (TFoot …)`, field-specific (`KFoot` = `SFoot ∨ NW ∨ SW`, plus `YW`), so `hw` can be proved INSIDE sc_frame (show
  t+3664 ∉ TFoot) with no caller change. `JAtZ.cs_frameI` (callers in 42 files) and `cs_frame` / `cs_frameB` / `cs_frameV` /
  `cs_frameIS` (~38 files) only know that FL4 wrote `OObj` words (VsTop `OObj` contains every TCB word in [t+256, t+4096), hence
  t+3664), so each IPC caller (XTopJoint{Send*,Recv*,Fault*,PushDon,...}, Ipc*) needs a finer footprint (e.g. `OObj` minus the
  VCPU word, proved from its P1 `WritesIn`). That is the bulk of the work: one cone batch for `vw` + sc_frame, then IPC caller
  batches. Alternative to consider first: a P1-level carried fact (P1's BlkOK / Cur0 family) that the TCB VCPU word is 0 for
  every TCB of `H.tcbs` (it already threads `plainW_all` per write), which would give `hw` uniformly from P1 posts.
- `live` at the carried ghosts: left for g2b (as the brief allowed).
- Boot: no lemma establishes `JAtZ` at an initial state in the tree, so `JExt`'s boot obligation is [W] for G4: the initial
  CSpace holds no VT-x cap (no Vcpu / Ept / EPT-mapped Frame / owned IoPort cap).

### (4) Findings
- [scope] `JVtxHypMU` / `JVtxScope` (an Untyped retype to a VT-x type 14..18; XTopJointKEntry20P / 23P) asks for `JAt` after the
  step. With `JAtZ.ext.nat` that post is unsatisfiable whenever such a retype succeeds (a Vcpu / Ept cap lands in a slot), so the
  scope premise now says outright "no successful VT-x retype" (was already out of scope: no spec counterpart). Consistent with G2
  `nativeScopeX`, but it is a premise false in a reachable state of a system that uses VT-x; the top is a native-only result.
- `JAtZ.ext` preservation needs NO premise across the native cone: nativeness is a property of the caps alone, and every native
  cap producer (retype `newCapOf`, IO-port issue, copies / mints / remaps) makes native caps.

### (5) Builds and axioms
- tokyo, FL4-sc mirror. ./g2a.sh (= g3e.sh). Targets (maximal modules of the edited cone's downstream closure): CapAlign DomAll
  IdleCovered IpcRS IpcReplyAll KsHeap Sc SpecInvCqD3 SpecInvCqGS SpecInvCqH3 SpecInvCqHC SpecInvEqT SpecInvNativeScopeBridge
  SpecInvRd8A4 SpecInvRd8bC SpecInvSgBridge SpecInvVfhG TcbPlace TopMCaps XTopJointKEntry28M XTopJointKEntry31 XTopJointPortInM.
- b1-b11 iterated module by module; b12 (~18 min) built the whole cone, failing only at XTopJointKEntry31:103 (a `simp` reshaping
  the `.Pml4` clause); r2 (fix: a definitional ascription) OK, 6590 jobs. No sorry / admit / native_decide / bv_decide in the
  diff. Root Fl4Proofs.lean (one import line) not rebuilt.
- Axioms (scratch/g2a/ax.lean, untracked): kernel_entryJ31, kernel_entryJ30, kernel_entryJ29G, JVtHyps.ofExt, vtAsid_ofR,
  JDelPartsN.toJ, KFinAtR31.to27, JAtZ.frVtJ, Vs.nativeCap_iff: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

### (6) Next (handoff)
- `vw` field + TCB-word frames (3) → `thr.obj` a theorem, `kernel_entryJ32` with `JDelPartsN` without `thr.obj`.
- `live`, then the other G2 joint (b) fields (INV-PLAN §4 list) in the same `JExt`, one cone batch each.

  pinned syscalls) with a ready head (OffReady), time does not advance inside the kernel. First phase = non-blocking,
  non-calling: ct ends Running (invPost) / Restart, or Inactive (it suspended itself: suspend keeps the binding and refills), never
  BlockedOn*; ct stays a TCB (detype needs a childless untyped, impossible in the same invocation that would delete ct's caps).
  ct unbound at the outcome (reply_remove's donation back to the caller, NBSendRecv donating to a passive receiver, SC unbind /
  SC cap deletion) ⇒ RT vacuous; ct still bound to cur_sc: refills untouched (ready head) except SchedControl configure of
  cur_sc (commit_time then refill_new / refill_update: head at cur_time, ready); ct cannot be re-bound (bind needs an unbound TCB,

  (SchedContextCap, final) runs sched_context_unbind_all_tcbs (ct unbound, reschedule_required) and sched_context_set_inactive
  (cur_sc: refills [], refill_max 0); cap_revoke's / rec_del's next preemption point fires and the syscall returns an error. The
  spec's `preemption_path` handles exactly this: ct is not `schedulable` (unbound), so it reads `sc_active cur_sc` = false and only
  sets consumed_time := 0 (no charge), then `maybe_handle_interrupt` — Rdy is not read there (no refill touched, no thread
  enqueued). The other error-outcome shapes: ct still schedulable (bound to cur_sc, never rebound by a deletion; cur_sc's refills
  untouched unless finalised, which unbinds ct) → check_budget / charge_budget with rd's `rd_chargeBudget` facts; ct not
  schedulable but cur_sc active (ct suspended / ct's TCB finalised, SC kept active) → charge_budget of an active cur_sc with no
  enqueue. So PreR needs, at the error outcomes: `schedulable ct → (cur_sc active with refills ∧ ct bound to cur_sc ∧ Excl ∧ ScFwd)`
  and `sc_active cur_sc → RV / Excl facts for charge_budget` plus Rdy across maybe_handle_interrupt (rd10's interrupt event);

## g2b (branch par/g2b in FL4-sc, on ad9e86d8 = int/j2 incl. g2a) — G2 second step: `JExt.vw` (every TCB's VCPU word 0); `JThreadFinHypsU.obj` proved; `kernel_entryJ32` (DONE); `live`: NOT done; JExt boot obligation stated
Goal (INV-PLAN §4 G2, Top risk 3; g2a handoff (3)/(6)): `JDelPartsN.thr.obj` [S] (∀-JAtZ: a slot's `Thread p` has `mem (p+3664) = 0`)
as a theorem of a carried fact; `live` at the carried ghosts if cheap; JExt's boot obligation as a [W] for G4.

### (1) P1-level fact: NOT feasible (checked)
- FL4 writes the TCB VCPU word (`layout::tcb::VCPU` = `NAME + NAME_LEN` = 3664) in exactly two places (crates/fl4-core/src/vcpu.rs):
  `vcpu::detach` (line ~701, writes 0) and the `X86VCPUSetTCB` arm of the VCPU invocation (line ~822, writes the VCPU pointer `v`).
  TCB creation (`objects::create_object` TCB arm: `init_context`, `init_fpu`, `debug::init_context`, `set_domain`,
  `set_child_name` (name bytes [3600, 3664)), `debug_append`) never writes it.
- P1 covers VT-x: `X86VCPUSetTCB` is a P1-reachable step and writes a non-zero word, so "every TCB's VCPU word is 0" is FALSE as a
  P1 invariant. P1's `KW` footprint (QueueFoot) and `BlkOK` treat 3664 as a plain TCB word (`plainW_all`); the native scope
  (no Vcpu cap) exists only at J (`JExt.nat`), which P1 does not see. A P1 version would have to be "VCPU word ≠ 0 → it names a
  live VCPU object bound back" plus "no VCPU objects", i.e. a BlkOK field re-proved across every P1 step and an H-vs-caps link
  (if_live_then_nonz_cap for VCPUs) that nothing carries: not feasible here.
- So the field is J-level, with the finer footprints g2a sized.

### (2) `JExt.vw` and the frames (JointAt)
- `JExt.vw : ∀ t, th t = some .tcb → L.mem s (tVcpuA t) = 0` [S] (`tVcpuA t = t + 3664`, ScKFoot). `VKeep th s s'` (every TCB's
  VCPU word kept); `JExt.of_eq` / `step` / `ss` now take `hv : VKeep`; `JExt.vkeep`, `JExt.mem`, `VKeep.of_writes` (from a
  `WritesIn` footprint missing every `tVcpuA`), `JAtZ.inSlot_nv` / `vkeep_slot` (slot words, `SlotsApart`), `JAtZ.ks_nv` /
  `ksW_nv` (the kernel-state block, P1 `ksOut`).
- Footprint vocabulary refined (no premise anywhere):
  * `Ipc.FinW` (IpcCancelSignals): the TCB clause's `K ≠ 3512` became `(K ≠ 3512 ∧ K ≠ 3664)` (producers prove it by `omega` on
    literal offsets; consumers use `.1`); `FinW.nv`.
  * `Sched.KFoot.ne_vcpu` (ScKeep; `SOffL` has no 3664), `tVcpuA_val` / `_aligned` / `tVcpuA_ne`.
  * `InT` (UntypedFrameBase, TCB creation words): the clause `t+3600 ≤ w` became `t+3600 ≤ w ∧ w ≠ t+3664` (every producer is an
    exact-offset write; the name loop stays below t+3656); `winZero_vcpu` (UtTcbRel): a new TCB's VCPU word is 0.
- Wrappers: `JAtZ.cs_frameI` / `cs_frameIS` / `JAtZR.cs_frameI` take `hWV : ∀ b, W b → ∀ t ∈ Z.T, b ≠ tVcpuA t` beside `hWO`
  (44 callers scripted: `Ipc.CnW.oobj` → `J.cnW_nv`, `Ipc.FinW.oobj` → `Ipc.FinW.nv`, `RmW.oobj` → `J.rmW_nv`; two WideW callers
  pass their exact one-word footprint); `JAtZ.cs_frame` / `JAtZR.cs_frame` / `JAtZ.sc_frameS` take `hv : VKeep`; `JAtZ.sc_frame`,
  `sch_frame`, `sc_frameR`, `JAtZR.sc_frame` / `sch_frame` derive it (`VKeep.of_tfoot`).
- Per-site keeps: restart (`JAtZ.vkeep_sts`, set_thread_state's `SFoot`), scheduler step (`schW_nv`), kernel-state steps (`ksW_nv`),
  debug list (`dbgWc_nv`), timer (`tmw_ne_tcb`), slot steps of the deletion loop / insert / grant / VSpace sub / TCB install
  (`vkeep_slot`), user / IPC-buffer / FPU / VSpace / VT-x frames (their existing `tcbK`), untyped zeroing (`hAp`), the eight retypes
  (old TCBs: slot footprint or window apart, `hWT`; UtCnRet: `thT_grow`; UtTcbRet: new TCBs by `winZero_vcpu`).

### (3) What became theorems
- `jThrObj_ofExt` (XTopJointKEntry32): `JThreadFinHypsU.obj` with NO premise (a slot's `Thread p` is valid, `SlotsValid.abs`, so
  `Z.th p = tcb`; then `J.ext.vw`).
- NEW TOP `kernel_entryJ32` = `kernel_entryJ31` with `hK : … → KDispHypsKV32` (`JEntryGlobM32.delParts : JDelPartsN32` =
  archRef / arKeep / ticks, all [P]). Wrappers `JDelPartsN32.toN`, `JEntryGlobM32.to31`, `KDispHypsKV32.to31`. J31 kept.
- So `JEntryGlobM32` holds no ∀-JAtZ premise any more (g3e (6)'s last two: `vt` g2a, `thr.obj` g2b).

### (4) `live` at the carried ghosts: NOT done (not cheap)
- `JEntryAt*.live` (INV-PLAN E15, ∀ H Cs Ac Lst D) is read in 22 files (all WJL deletions and installs) and its per-state form
  needs `LiveDN` carried across every step (INV-PLAN's L item, no machinery outside the deletion loop's WJL). Re-scoping only the
  quantifier would need the carried ghosts as parameters of `JEntryAtR2` and of the whole dispatch chain. Not cheap: left as is
  ([J] ∀-ghosts), next line's work.

### (5) JExt's boot obligation ([W] for G4)
- For the initial joint state (s0, a0, σ0) with ghosts Z0: `JExt Z0.th s0` =
  (nat) every slot of `Z0.th` holds a `Vs.NativeCap`: no `Vcpu`, no `Ept`, no `Frame` with mapped ∧ EPT flag, no `IoPort` with
  owner ≠ 0; and (vw) every TCB of `Z0.th` has its VCPU word `mem (t + 3664) = 0`.
  Following the 2026-11-20 lead decision (G4 starts from any state satisfying the carried invariants), this is part of the
  `BootJ` premise of `jreach_inv`; for a concrete FL4 boot state it holds because the boot code creates no VT-x object and every TCB
  is created zeroed (`InT`/`winZero_vcpu` for retyped TCBs; the root task's TCB from zeroed memory).

### (6) Findings
- No premise false in reachable native states was added. `JExt.vw` is preserved by every native step of the cone (no new premise).
- [scope, as g2a] a successful VT-x step (`X86VCPUSetTCB`) breaks `vw` (it writes a non-zero word); it is already outside the scope
  (`JExt.nat`: no Vcpu cap, so the invocation cannot be reached at J).
- The footprints were coarser than the kernel: P3's `FinW` / `InT` admitted the VCPU word although no native code writes it;
  refining them cost no proof beyond `omega` (the writes are at literal offsets). P1's `KW` still admits it (left unchanged: the
  J-level frames do not need it).

### (7) Builds and axioms
- tokyo, FL4-sc mirror (warm), ./g2b.sh (= g2a.sh). Targets: the 20 maximal modules of the downstream closure of the edited files
  (954 modules): DomAll IdleCovered IpcRS IpcReplyAll KsHeap Sc SpecInvEqT SpecInvNativeScopeBridge SpecInvRd12bD SpecInvRd8cD
  SpecInvRd8fC SpecInvRd8gG SpecInvSgBridge SpecInvVfhG TcbPlace TopMCaps XTopJointKEntry28M XTopJointKEntry30D XTopJointKEntry32
  XTopJointPortInM.
- b1 (~23 min): everything upstream of XTopJointStep OK; 2 errors (explicit `arI` section variable). b2: 2 errors (an anonymous
  `JExt` in UtDropJ2; SendBlockG's local restatement of `FinW`'s clause, same in 11 files). b3: 2 errors (`JAtZR.cnW_nv` missing).
  b4: "Build completed successfully (6712 jobs)". No sorry / admit / native_decide / bv_decide in the diff. Root Fl4Proofs.lean
  (one import line) not rebuilt.
- Axioms (scratch/g2b/ax.lean, untracked; task g2b-ax1): kernel_entryJ32, kernel_entryJ31, kernel_entryJ30, jThrObj_ofExt,
  JDelPartsN32.toN, KDispHypsKV32.to31, JExt.step, VKeep.of_writes, VKeep.of_tfoot, JAtZ.cs_frameI, Ipc.FinW.nv, winZero_vcpu,
  JAtZ.mp_vkeep: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

### (8) Next (handoff)
- `live` at the carried ghosts (INV-PLAN E15), then the other G2 joint (b) fields in the same `JExt`.

  `BC` (cur_sc's holder is ct) is NOT invariant over the deletion cone, and Rdy is still kept there: the caller is
  BlockedOnReply at the donation and Inactive right after (`replyUnlinkTcb`), hence not queued / switch target / BlkR. That

  there by ctq18's `eb_fl4HandleEvent_err`): `CurHold` alone is not stepwise invariant, because `restart_thread_if_no_fault`
  (IpcCancel `restartThreadIfNoFault`: Restart, i.e. runnable, plus `possibleSwitchTo`, no state read) and
  `remove_and_restart_ntfn_queued_thread` (Restart with no fault check) make a non-ct thread runnable. The argument at those

## g2c (branch par/g2c in FL4-sc, on 895055b2 = int/j2 incl. g2b) — G2 third step: `JEntryAt.live` re-scoped to the carried ghosts; `live` out of `hK`, asked once at the entry state and carried to the dispatch state; `kernel_entryJ33` (DONE); the carry from the dispatch state to the exit (the post) NOT done (handoff)
Goal (INV-PLAN §1 E15, §3, §4 G2; g2b handoff (4)/(8)): make `live` (∀-ghost [J], read in 22 files) a per-state carried fact.
Resumed once (predecessor cut off after ~10 min with the re-scope of (1) uncommitted; kept as is, it built unchanged).

### (1) Re-scope of the field (commit d2c5a35d)
- `JEntryAt` (XTopJointEntry), `JEntryAtR` (KEntry27), `JEntryAtR2` (KEntry27b) take the ghosts `H Cs` as parameters; `live` was
  `∀ H Cs Ac Lst D, JAtZ … s ar σ → LiveDN Z.th H Cs Z.G s σ`, it is now `LiveDN Z.th H Cs Z.G s σ`.
- Every reader (`have hLv := hE.live H Cs Ac Lst D J` in decOK_J, KEntry13P/17P/18P/23P) instantiated the ∀ at the `JAtZ` it decodes
  from, so the readers changed to `hE.live` only. The dispatch chain (JEntryHyps, dispatch_invokeJ / JE / JPI / JEPI / JEPZEC(I) /
  JAll, invoke_afterJ, handle_invocation_entryJ, KDispHyps 8..32 bundles, Preempt*) passes the ghosts it already has (`H Cs` of the
  decode's JAtZ): 59 files, one token each. No new premise; every top's `hK` got strictly weaker (J32's statement keeps its shape).
- So INV-PLAN §3's row "`JEntryAt.live` … false at a non-reachable instance: possibly (LiveDN at another heap H' that also satisfies
  JAtZ)" is resolved: the field no longer quantifies over ghosts.

### (2) `kernel_entryJ33` (commit 0ea2bd12, new leaf XTopJointKEntry33)
- `LiveDN.of_keep`: `LiveDN` kept at the same ghosts by a step keeping the slots (`SlotsSame`), the debug words (`DbgKeep`), every TCB's
  `affA` / `stA` / `scA` / `boundA` / `yieldA` word, the action and idle words and `isOriginalCap` (`LiveJ.of_sameZ`: a TCB zombie's
  object is a TCB by `DelInv.zwf`/`ZOK`, so its `DeadP` reads only those words; `DbgWFL.of_keep`; `NullOrig.of_same`). This is the
  generic frame for every step family whose footprint misses those words (the analogue of g2a/g2b's `JExt.of_eq` / `VKeep`).
- `budget_ok_frT` (passing `budget_ok` writes the current node's CUR_TIME / CONSUMED only: XTopJointPP `update_timestamp_fr` +
  P1 `check_budget_restart.same`), `front_writes` (KFrontB writes those two words and the current TCB's FAULT_IP register, offset 392),
  `BudgetAt.orig` (the spec front keeps the original bits), `liveDN_front` (LiveDN at the entry ⇒ LiveDN at every dispatch state `hK`
  is asked at: ghosts `Z.mv Z.G V'`, `H`, `Cs`, FL4 state `KFrontB`, spec state `BudgetAt σ σb true`).
- `JEntryAtR3` / `KDispHypsKV33` (= `JEntryAtR2` / `KDispHypsKV32` without `live`), `.toR2` / `.to32 hLv`.
- `kernel_entryJ33` = `kernel_entryJ32` with `hK : … → KDispHypsKV33` and ONE new per-state premise
  `hLv : LiveDN Z.th H Cs Z.G s σ` [J] (l4v `if_unsafe_then_cap`, `if_live_then_nonz_cap`, `zombies_final`, `valid_nullcaps`, FL4's
  debug-list shape) at the entry state and the entry JAtZ's own ghosts. J32 kept (J33 is a wrapper over it).

### (3) Step families: which keep `LiveDN` (b)
- Proved: the FL4 front (FAULT_IP + passing budget_ok, `liveDN_front`); inside an invocation, existing (pre-g2c) lemmas already
  carry it: the caller's restart (`WJL.restart`), the whole deletion loop at `WJL` (`wjl_keep` and the WJL step lemmas: slot swaps /
  zombie writes / empties, every finaliser incl. a thread cap's `debug_remove`, preemption point, post deletion), a TCB install's
  insert (`LiveDN.insT`).
- NOT done (what G4 needs: LiveDN at the exit state, in the post `KPost`/`RJ`): every family from the dispatch state to the exit,
  through the J decode lemmas' posts (they end at `JAt`, which does not carry LiveDN):
  (i) the deletion / install invocations: the WJL invariant already holds LiveDN at their end (`EJL`/`WJL` posts), so only the plumbing
  to the decode post is missing (S–M);
  (ii) IPC (send / recv / reply / fault / grant transfer): slots change only by the grant's insert (a cap alike the sender's: shape of
  `LiveDN.insT`), TCB states change (DeadP of a TCB zombie's TCB: dead TCBs are not IPC partners), no debug words: `LiveDN.of_keep`
  plus an insert lemma (M);
  (iii) retype / reset: new objects' slots null, new TCBs appended to the debug list together with their thread cap (`dbg` needs the
  cap: holds after the retype loop, not between `debug_append` and the cap insert) (M–L);
  (iv) VSpace map / unmap / pool, CNode copy / mint / move / mutate / rotate, IRQ / IO control, SchedControl / SC / TCB config:
  slot writes of caps alike existing ones (`RefsObj` only sees CNode / Thread / Zombie caps; copies of those are alike) (M);
  (v) `finish` (schedule, activate_thread, timer / release): footprints miss slots and debug words; DeadP of dead TCBs kept because
  dead TCBs are never scheduled (S–M, `LiveDN.of_keep` with `JAtZ.deadP_keep`).
  Cost: one cone pass (the J decode posts are in ~100 modules) if LiveDN is added as a `JExt` field with `JExt.of_eq` / `step` taking
  the `LiveDN.of_keep` inputs; or a separate post field on `JAt` (same cone).
- No step found that breaks LiveDN in native scope (no FINDING).

### (4) Boot obligation ([W] for G4, per the 2026-11-20 lead decision)
- For the initial joint state (s0, a0, σ0) with ghosts Z0, H0, Cs0: `LiveDN Z0.th H0 Cs0 Z0.G s0 σ0`: every slot in use of a CNode or
  TCB of Z0.th is covered by an MDB cap (CNode / Thread / Zombie) naming its container; every TCB on core 0's debug list is named by a
  thread cap; zombie conditions (no zombies at boot: vacuous); the debug lists well formed (`DbgWF` with the TCBs of H0, cores Cs0);
  no null slot original. Part of `BootJ` beside JExt's (g2b (5)); for a concrete FL4 boot state it holds because the root task's
  CNode / TCB are named by the root caps, its TCB is the only debug-list member and boot makes no zombie.

### (5) Findings
- None false in reachable native states. The old ∀-ghost form was the risky one (INV-PLAN §3); the new field and `hLv` are per-state.

### (6) Builds and axioms
- tokyo, FL4-sc mirror (warm), ./g2c.sh (= g2b.sh). r1 (re-scope; targets = the 4 maximal modules of the 144-module downstream
  closure of the 59 edited files: XTopJointKEntry28M XTopJointKEntry30D XTopJointKEntry32 XTopJointPortInM): "Build completed

  No sorry / admit / native_decide / bv_decide in the diff.

  budget_ok_frT, BudgetAt.orig, KDispHypsKV33.to32, decOK_J, dispatch_invokeJAll: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

### (7) Next (handoff)

## g2d (branch par/g2d in FL4-sc, on c03735fa = int/j2 incl. g2c, kernel_entryJ33, rd8p) — G2 fourth step: carry `LiveDN` from dispatch to exit. STOPPED on a FINDING: `LiveDN` (J33's `hLv` [J]) is false in reachable native states; families (a)–(f) NOT started (carrying it would prove nothing until `LiveJ` is re-scoped)
Goal (g2c handoff (3)(i)–(v), (7)): LiveDN at the exit as a JExt / JAtZR field, `kernel_entryJ34` without `hLv`.

### (1) FINDING (commit 43bf8ab0, new leaf XTopJointLiveFalse, root imports it)
`LiveDN Z.th H Cs Z.G s σ` = `LiveJ ∧ DbgWF ∧ NullOrig` is refuted at any `JAtZ` state with `SpecGlob σ`
(l4v valid_global_refs; SInvB carries it as SpecGlobS, and every deletion carries it in WJ) in two situations
every FL4 system reaches:
- `liveDN_idle_off` / `not_liveDN_of_idle`: `LiveJ.dbg` asks a thread cap of the MDB naming every TCB on core 0's
  debug list; `SpecGlob.idle` says no cap (but a frame cap) names the idle thread (`JAtZ.idleThread_eq`); so under
  LiveDN the idle thread is NOT on core 0's debug list. FL4 puts it there at boot and never removes it:
  crates/fl4-core/src/boot.rs `init_core_state` (l.684-693) appends every core's idle thread to its core's list
  when `fl4_abi::config::DEBUG_BUILD` (= `true`, Fl4Core/Funs.lean:1414); `create_idle_thread` sets core 0's
  idle affinity 0; `debug_remove` is called only from a thread cap's finalisation (objects.rs) and `migrate_tcb`
  (smp.rs), neither reaches the idle thread (no cap names it, no SC rebinding). So `hLv` is false at EVERY state
  reachable from FL4's boot. l4v's `if_live_then_nonz_cap` exempts the idle thread (IdleThreadState is not `live`).
- `liveDN_irqNode_free` / `not_liveDN_of_irqNode`: `LiveJ.slots` asks a CNode / thread / zombie cap of the MDB
  naming the container of every slot in use; IRQ `i`'s node slot is slot 0 of the radix-0 CNode `nodeA kb i` of
  the typed heap (`IntLayout.node`), which `SpecGlob.ref` (+ `IrqRel.node`) says no non-frame cap names; so under
  LiveDN every IRQ node slot is unused. The step that breaks it: IRQHandler `SetIRQHandler`
  (interrupt.rs `decode_irq_handler`, l.70-83: `cdt::insert(s, cap, slot, irq_slot)` of the notification cap;
  spec `invokeIRQHandler` `capInsert`). Every state after a successful SetIRQHandler violates LiveDN. l4v's
  `if_unsafe_then_cap` covers an IRQ node slot by the IRQ handler cap (`cte_refs (IRQHandlerCap irq)` =
  {irq node slot}, `appropriate_cte_cap` of a notification cap = True).
- Consequences: `kernel_entryJ33` (hLv), and every earlier top through `JEntryAt.live` / `JEntryAtR(2).live`
  (∀-ghost before g2c, per-state since), are vacuous on boot-reachable states. The proofs that read LiveDN (WJL:
  every CNode Delete / Revoke, the TCB installs, the IRQ handler deletion) are sound but vacuous there. g2c's
  boot obligation (4) ("its TCB is the only debug-list member") was wrong: the idle threads are members too.
  No other part found false: `zslots` / `zdead` / `DbgWF` / `NullOrig` were not refuted (DbgWF needs the idle
  TCB among `H.tcbs`; not checked further).

### (2) Fix (re-scope of `LiveJ`, XTopJointLive; size M, deletion cone; NOT done here)
- `slots`: add the disjunct "the slot lies in the kernel-state block": `IsSlotAt th q i → InUse … (slotOf q i) →
  (∃ y ∈ G.chains.flatten, RefsObj q (capV y)) ∨ (ksb ≤ (slotOf q i).val ∧ (slotOf q i).val < ksb + 13568)`.
  Its consumer is already shaped for it: `SlotLiveAt` (XTopJointEmptyUt) has the same block disjunct, and
  `JAtZ.delUtFact_of` handles it (`omega` against `jcov.ks`). Carry sites need `L.ksb s' = L.ksb s` (every
  `DbgKeep` has it as `.1`, `WritesIn` as `.1`).
- `dbg`: exempt the idle thread: `dbgNth … ≠ 0 → dbgNth … ≠ L.idleW s → ∃ y ∈ G…, capV y = .Thread …`.
  Consumers: `ReadyLive`'s second part (`head ≠ 0 → head ≠ idleW → OtherCov …`) and `delUtFact_of`'s head case
  (the idle head is outside every RAM untyped region by `J.jcov.idleOut`, `IdleAt` left disjunct),

  `≠ idleW` case, same `idleOut` argument in `DbgSuccCov`'s consumer, or exempt there too). Carry sites need the
  idle word kept: `IdleKeep` (`JAtZ.idleW_keep`) — LiveJ.of_same / of_sameZ, WJL, WJLSwap, WJLEmpty, WJLFinT,
  WJLIns (insT), FinThreadU: 17 field reads in 10 files (grep `hL.dbg\|hL.slots`).
- Alternative closer to l4v for `slots`: cover an IRQ node slot by an `IrqHandler i` cap of the MDB
  (cte_refs); costlier (the IRQ handler deletion must then keep the handler cap until the node slot is emptied:
  that is FL4's order in `deleted_irq_handler`, but WJL's readiness would need the new case). The block
  disjunct is what the consumers already accept, so it is the cheap choice.
- After the re-scope, `liveDN_idle_off` / `liveDN_irqNode_free` become non-refutations (keep them as checks
  that the exemptions are needed) and g2c's plan (3)(i)–(v) applies unchanged.

### (1) Re-scope of `LiveJ` (commit 46383948; XTopJointLive and 16 cone files, one batch)
- `LiveJ.slots`: `IsSlotAt th q i → InUse … (slotOf q i) → (∃ y ∈ G…, RefsObj q (capV y)) ∨ KsSlot (L.ksb s) (slotOf q i)`,
  `KsSlot kb y := kb.val ≤ y.val ∧ y.val < kb.val + 13568` (new abbrev = `SlotLiveAt`'s right disjunct). l4v: an IRQ node slot
  is covered by the IRQ state / handler cap (`cte_refs (IRQHandlerCap irq)`), not by a CNode cap.
- `LiveJ.dbg`: `dbgNth … ≠ 0 → (dbgNth …).bv ≠ σ.idleThread → ∃ thread cap` (l4v `if_live_then_nonz_cap`: the idle thread is
  not `live`). Exemption by the SPEC idle thread, not the FL4 idle word: at a `JAtZ` state they are the same
  (`JAtZ.idleThread_bv`, a local copy of DelR's `idleThread_eq`; `JAtZ.bv_ne_idleThread`), and the carry then needs only
  `σ'.idleThread = σ.idleThread`, which every deletion step gives for free (SpecGlobFK's `GK` family; `gk_idle`, new in
  XTopJointWJL) or `CnK` (`Ipc.CnK.idle`, new in XTopJointLive), instead of `IdleKeep` from two `JAtZ` + SchedRel
  (`JAtZ.idleW_keep`). The head consumers still use the FL4 word and `JCovD.idleOut` as planned.
- Consumers:
  - `ReadyLive`'s second part: `dbgHead ≠ 0 → dbgHead ≠ L.idleW s → OtherCov …`; `JAtZ.readyLive` (block case `Or.inr`,
    idle via `bv_ne_idleThread`).
  - `JAtZ.delUtFact_of` (XTopJointEmptyUt): `hdbg` asks `head ≠ idleW`; the idle head is outside every RAM untyped region by
    `J.jcov.idleOut` (left disjunct of `IdleAt`). The block case of `hlive` was already handled.
  - `LiveOther` (XTopJointWJL) got both exemptions; `LiveJ.liveOther` propagates them; `emptyHypJL` rebuilds `LiveJ`.
  - XTopJointFinThreadU: `DbgSuccCov T G w s` asks the successor `≠ w`; `dbgSuccCov_of_live` gives it at `w = L.idleW s`;
    new `JAtZ.dbgRemoveJI` (copy of XTopJointFinThread's `dbgRemoveJ`, left untouched to keep it out of the cone) handles the
    idle successor by `idleOut` (debug_append pushes at the head, so the idle thread is the LAST entry of core 0's list and
    can be the removed head's successor); `finThreadJU` transports `L.idleW s6 = L.idleW s` (σ6 after `suspend`:
    `gk_suspend'`, `JAtZ.idleThread_bv` at both ends).
- Carry sites (the 17 field reads in 10 files of g2d (2), plus their callers): `LiveJ.of_same` / `of_sameZ` take
  `hid : σ'.idleThread = σ.idleThread` (the block case by `DbgKeep.1`: ksb kept); `LiveJ.of_sameDbg` takes `hid` and
  `hks`; `wjl_keep` takes `hid` (callers: `gk_finaliseCap` at the finaliser's spec outcome, `rfl` for the VT-x finalisers
  and the IPC-buffer write, `stsAct` by `split <;> rfl` for the restart); zombie write (`gk_setCap`), empty
  (`hnk.idle`), swap (`hnk.idle`), insert `LiveDN.insT` (`hcn.idle`); preemption point (`gke_preemptionPoint'`, WJLPP and
  MRDel), post deletion (`KsStep.idle`), TCB install's reschedule (`gk_rescheduleRequired'`); `LiveDN.of_keep` takes
  `hid`, `liveDN_front` gives it by `BudgetAt.shape27`.
- No premise added anywhere; every changed lemma's inputs are facts the call sites already had.

### (2) The refutations no longer apply (XTopJointLiveFalse rewritten; root import unchanged)
- `liveJ_dbg_idle`: at a `JAtZ` state, `dbg`'s premise fails at a debug-list entry equal to the idle word.
- `irqNode_ksSlot`: every IRQ node slot `slotOf (nodeA kb i) 0` is an `IsSlotAt` slot inside the block (`nodeA_val`), so
  `slots` holds there with no cap.
- `LiveJ.of_l4v`: `LiveJ` from l4v-shaped facts silent on the idle thread and the IRQ node: a cap for every slot in use whose
  container is no IRQ node CNode, a thread cap for every debug-listed TCB other than the idle word, the zombie facts. So
  `LiveJ` holds with core 0's idle thread on the debug list and with any IRQ node slots in use.
- Corrected boot obligation [W] for G4 (replaces g2c (4)): `LiveBootW s σ` = the inputs of `of_l4v` + `DbgWF` +
  `NullOrig`; `liveDN_of_boot : JAtZ → LiveBootW → LiveDN`. At FL4's boot: the root CNode / root TCB named by the root
  caps; the idle threads (every core's, on their lists) exempt; IRQ node slots null (no handler at boot) but exempt anyway;
  no zombie; no null original slot.
- g2d's `liveDN_idle_off` / `liveDN_irqNode_free` / `not_liveDN_of_*` are gone (their statements are false now; the three
  lemmas above are the checks that the exemptions are needed and suffice).
- One-core note [S]: the exemption is the spec's (= the current core's) idle thread; `dbg` reads core 0's list, so on a
  core `c ≠ 0` core 0's idle thread would still be uncovered. FL4's native scope is one core (`Z.c = 0` is already a [P]
  path premise, INV-PLAN P7/P12), so no premise false in native-scope states.

  `jPreemptHypLL : PPHypDW (WJL) (WJPL)` (the preemption point writes time words only; `LiveJ.of_sameZ` with

### rd14e-2 (par/rd14e reset to 4aabd427 = int/j2 incl. rd14e A–C, rd8w) — lead decision on the FINDING, option (a): `OS` gains a third disjunct; `TW` widened; the consumer handles it
- **`OI σ := cur_sc ≠ idle_sc ∧ (∀ y n, kheap cur_sc = SC y n → scActive y = false) ∧ action ≠ resume`** (SpecInvRdY) and
  **`OS σ := (OffReady ∧ Suff) ∨ (consumed = 0 ∧ action ≠ resume) ∨ OI σ`** (SpecInvRdK). `OffReady` unchanged. The extra conjunct
  `cur_sc ≠ idle_sc` is NEEDED (not a weakening elsewhere): if cur_sc were the idle SC and inactive, `schedule` could pick idle,
  `p = cur_sc`, `switch_sched_context` would not set the reprogram flag, `commit_time` would not run, and the stale consumed time
  would break `OffReady` at exit. In the deletion scenario it holds (ct ≠ idle is bound to cur_sc; ValidIdle: no non-idle thread is
  bound to the idle SC) — but it is not in `BS` / `EF` / the arm interfaces, see handoff.

  precondition gains `∨ (scActive x = false ∧ p ≠ cur_sc)` (p ≠ cur_sc ⇒ the reprogram flag is set ⇒ commit_time runs ⇒ consumed 0 ⇒

  `preemption_path`: ct schedulable (case i, cur_sc active): `check_budget` — `Suff` ⇒ `p` unchanged, `SS4` by rd14d's `ss4_tt`

## g2i (branch par/g2i in FL4-sc, on 9f508a65 = int/j2 incl. g2h) — G2 ninth step, the FIELD route (lead decision): batch (1) in two committed parts (LiveDN's definitions upstream of `JointAt`; runJ = runJD's corollary; the field-free frame infrastructure); the field `JAtZ.live` itself and the construction sites (batch (2)) NOT committed: a work-in-progress patch and the exact remaining list below; kernel_entryJ34 (batch (3)) NOT started
Goal: g2h (3)'s plan as the lead fixed it: `LiveDN` (at the JAtZ's own ghosts) a field of `JAtZ`; each construction proves it where
its dead set and frames are visible; then `kernel_entryJ34` without `hLv`. Commits b6df4ec8 (batch 1a) and 2d11464d (batch 1b). No premise
added to any committed theorem, no new axiom.

### (1) Batch 1a (commit b6df4ec8): the definitions upstream of `JointAt`
- `JAtZ` cannot mention `LiveDN` where it was defined: `LiveJ` (XTopJointLive), `DbgWF` (DbgWF), `NullOrig` (XTopJointNullOrig),
  `ZTcb` (XTopJointLiveKeep) and `LiveDN` (XTopJointWJLRestart) all lie in `JointAt`'s downstream cone. New module `LiveDefs`
  (imported by `JointAt`; imports `JointAt`'s imports and `P1.QueueDbgKeep`) holds them, moved unchanged (P1 names qualified):
  RefsObj, InUse, dbgNth, KsSlot, dbgHead, LiveJ; nextIn, prevA, DbgWFL, DbgWF, DbgWFL.congr, dbgHd, DbgWFs, dbgHd_of_ksb;
  NullOrig, NullOrig.notInUse, NullOrig.of_same, orig_eq_of_slots; dbgNth_keep, LiveJ.of_same, ZTcb, LiveJ.ztcb, LiveJ.of_sameZ,
  DbgWFL.of_keep; LiveDN. Full names unchanged, so no user changed.
- `JAtZ.runJD` moved from the leaf XTopJointLiveSt into XTopJointReply; `JAtZ.runJ` is now `WP.spec_mono (J.runJD …)` (g2h (1)'s
  "fold runJD back").

### (2) Batch 1b (commit 2d11464d): field-free infrastructure the construction sites need
- JointAt: `XTopAt.idleThread_bv` (the spec's idle thread is the idle word at any `XTopAt` state), `LiveJ.regh` (`LiveJ` at another
  MDB tree of the same slots: the trees' members are the non-null slots), `ZTcb.of_same`, and **`liveDN_frame`**: `LiveDN` at
  `(s', σ')` and at the ghost tree `Z'.G` of any `XTopAt` after, from `LiveDN` at `(s, σ)`, `SlotsSame`, P1's `DbgKeep`, the original
  bits and the idle word kept, and the TCB zombies' TCBs `DeadP` after. No `JAtZ` after is needed (g2f's `LiveDN.of_jstep` needed
  `J'`), so it serves inside the constructions.
- XTopJointFinW / XTopJointJAtZRA: `JAtZ.kw_dbgKeep` / `JAtZR.kw_dbgKeep` (P1's `KW` footprint keeps every debug word: the full
  `DbgKeep`, next to `kw_dbg`'s core-0 head word).
- ScChargeH: `JHole.dbgK : P1.DbgKeep … s0 s` (every debug word kept from the base; `update_timestamp` writes two time words of
  the current node: `dbgW_not_kw`), `JHole.dbgK_node` (one more time-word write: the consumed-time reset); the four `JHole`
  constructions (timestampJH, XTopJointPreempt, XTopJointMRPath4, XTopJointPreemptI) and `JAtZ.toHole` (XTopJointPPH) supply it.

### (3) FINDINGS (why batch (2) is larger than "one proof per construction")
- (F1) No coarse footprint of the J layer excludes the debug words: `OObj` (TCB words 256..4096, whole node), `KFoot`/`TFoot`
  (`SFoot` covers the whole current node, its `+88` debug head included), `FinW`/`CnW` (TCB offsets 256..4096 but 3440/3472/3512/
  3664, so 3576/3584 `DEBUG_NEXT/PREV` included). So `DbgKeep` (needed for `LiveJ.dbg` and `DbgWF`) never follows from the
  frames the constructions already use; it comes from P1's `KW` footprint (`hfoot`), which most sites hold as
  `have hDbg := J.kw_dbg hfoot` (60 such sites: `have hKd := J.kw_dbgKeep hfoot` added after each in the WIP).
- (F2) Interfaces that carry only the core-0 debug head (`kw_dbg`'s form) must be widened to `DbgKeep`:
  `JHole` (done, A2), `ScStepP1` ([P], the SC paths' `JSchedCPath/JSchedCtxPath.rest`: WIP adds a `DbgKeep` conjunct — still
  true: an SC decode writes no debug word), `SchTailHyps` (WIP: field `dbgK`, P1's `SchedW` footprint keeps every debug word,
  `P1.dbgKeep_schedW`), `JTH` (the timeout hole, ScChargeT/TA/TR: not done), `restartTailJ`'s and `suspendJ`'s continuations
  (`∀ Ac' hblk hDbg`, XTopJointRestart:574, XTopJointSuspend: not done), `rbw_dbg` (RBW footprint, the receive-signal family:
  needs `rbw_dbgKeep`, a field-offset case analysis: not done).
- (F3) The dead set shrinks at some constructions (`sc_kern` takes `D' ⊆ D`): SC Bind drops the bound TCB / notification
  (ScJointStep:620), `undead` / `undeadC` (a thread / reply leaves `D` when covered), TcbSsp's `{q ∈ D | q ≠ sc, t}`,
  `D \ {ptr}` (ScChargeT/TA, SendBlockG). So `zD` (below) is per site: the dropped object is no TCB zombie's TCB. Lemmas (WIP):
  `JAtZ.ztcb_tcb` (a TCB zombie's object is a TCB of `th`, `DelInv.zwf`), `JAtZ.not_ztcb` (an object named by a non-zombie cap of a
  slot is no TCB zombie's, `FinInv.zombie_alone`), `JAtZ.replyArg_ntcb`. Each needed only facts in scope; no premise.
- (F4) No step found that breaks `LiveDN` in native scope; no premise false in reachable states added. The one genuinely new
  proof still missing is g2f's retype loop invariant (`debug_append` before the thread-cap insert).

### (4) The field design (WIP, `proofs/scratch/g2i/B-wip.patch`, untracked; applies on 2d11464d)
- `JAtZ.live : LiveDN Z.th H Cs Z.G s σ` and `JAtZ.zD : ∀ p ∈ ZTcb Z.th s, p ∈ D` (the TCB zombies' TCBs are in the dead set; true in
  every state since `live.zdead` makes them `DeadP` and `D ∪ ZTcb` is a dead set: `addDeadSet`). With `zD`, a frame site gets
  `LiveJ.zdead` after from the post's own `jcov.dead` (every site already proves the dead set dead after), no per-word TCB frame.
  `JAtZR`, `JAtZS` get both fields (their conversions copy them).
- `JAtZ.liveX` / `JAtZR.liveX` (= `liveDN_frame` at `J`), `zDX`.
- Constructors: `cs_frameV`/`cs_frame`/`cs_frameB` (JAtZ, JAtZR) take `hlv : LiveDN … G' s' σ'` and `hzD` (the slot-changing steps
  prove their own: deletion (WJL has it), insert (`LiveDN.insG/insC/wstep`), …); `cs_frameI`/`cs_frameIS` (slots kept) and the SC frames
  `sc_frame`, `sch_frame`, `sc_frameR`, `sc_frameS`, `JAtZR.sc_frame/sch_frame` take `hKd : DbgKeep`, `hidl` (idle word kept; or
  `horig` for `cs_frameI`) and `hDD : ∀ p ∈ ZTcb Z.th s, p ∈ D'`, and build `live` by `liveX`.
- Patched by script in the WIP (the arguments were in scope): 33 `cs_frameI` sites (`hKd`, the `irel_same` original-bit
  equality, `J.idleW_keep …`.1, `J.zD`), 23 `sc_frame`, 3 `sc_frameR`, 5 `sc_frameS`, 4 `sch_frame`, `addDeadSet`, `addDead`,
  `undead`, `undeadC` (+ 12 callers).

### (3) The induction (XTopJointKEntry35)
- **`JReach arI AR MR : S → A → State Unit → Prop`**: `start` — any `JAtZ … s a σ` (some ghosts), `SInvX σ`, `MR a σ.machineState`

  `handle_syscall st arI s a n = ok (s', a')`, `((), σ') ∈ (fl4KernelEntrySyscall true c σ).1`, `RJ s' a' σ'`, and
  `MR a' σ'.machineState` (the open carry T4: KPost does not give it, so `step` asks it of the exit).
- **`jreach_inv (hnd)`**: `JReach s a σ → (∃ ghosts, JAtZ … s a σ) ∧ SInvX σ ∧ MR a σ.machineState` (JAtZ from RJ's JAt, which
  carries `live` / `zD` / `ext` as fields; SInvX by `kentry_sinvX`).
- **`kernel_entry_reach`** (the [P] bundle + `hRef hPI`, `hnd`): `JReach s a σ → ∃ ghosts, JAtZ ∧ SInvX σ ∧ MR ∧ ∀ n c, ct ≠ idle →
  NativeSys n c → hflag → hK (at those ghosts) → hFin → hFast → handle_syscall ⦃ r => spec fails ∨ ∃ σ', outcome ∧ RJ r σ' ∧
  SInvX σ' ∧ (MR r.2 σ'.machineState → JReach r.1 r.2 σ') ⦄`. So the bundle is inductive up to the MR carry: every related exit
  is again a start-shaped state (JAtZ from RJ, SInvX from the spec carry), and with MR it is reachable.

  (E4–E10, P1, P7, P9, P10, the Untyped / device [J] fields) and hFin (F1, F6) asked at each reachable state's ghosts, and the two
  induction gaps (G-a) spec no-fail, (G-b) the MR carry to the exit.

`kernel_entryJ13PUG`'s three exits: (i) the stopping budget check (`checkBudget` false, then `finish`), (ii) the dispatch's ok
outcomes then `finish`, (iii) the dispatch's preempted outcomes (`PPQJI`) then `finish` from the preemption path. `MR` holds at
the entry (`hR`) and after the FaultIP write + budget check (`budget_mr_at`, already in 13P); it was dropped by `finish` and by
the dispatch posts.
- **FL4 side, `finish` keeps `MR`** (MachKeepF, arch only): `MKD.syscall_finish` and the call graph below it (`schedule`,
  `activate_thread`, `timer_fire(_loop)`, `awaken`, the switch / choose / next-interrupt / switch-sched-context steps,
  `smp_send_pending`), generated by the `mkd_walk` of MachKeepD (scripts scratch/mr6/topo.py + mkdgen.py on
  scratch/g4b/fin_gen.txt): every arch op reached is a field of `MRKeepD` or a pure query. Also `MKD.syscall_handle_recv`,
  `MKD.syscall_handle_yield` (+ the IPC / notification / fault / budget functions under them).
- **spec side, `finish` keeps the four machine fields `MR` reads** (MachFieldFamS): `MachT.mtk_*G` per scheduler function

### (2) The one new carry: `JDispMR` [W] (XTopJointKEntry36)
`JDispMR s a σ n c := MR a σ.ms → dispatch_syscall s a n ⦃ r => DispPostR … (PPQJI) (fl4HandleSyscall true c) σ r →
DispPostRM … MR … σ r ⦄`: a dispatch run related to some spec outcome is related to one where `MR` also holds. Pointwise and
existential on purpose: at `State Unit` the spec is nondeterministic in the oracle positions (`orChoiceE` of
`preemptionPoint` via `StateExt.wrapExtBool`), so "every related outcome has `MR`" is false (two outcomes differing in
`timeState` / `irqState`); only the outcome the FL4 run matches has it (l4v: shared machine state, each `do_machine_op` matched
by `corres`). Asked at the same states as `hK` (σb after FaultIP + passing budget check, at a `KFrontB` FL4 state with
`JAtZ`), not ∀ states.
- **Narrowed** (XTopJointKEntry37): `JDispMR.of_keep` (FL4 dispatch keeps `MR` + spec branch keeps the fields and never fails
  ⇒ `JDispMR`); `dispatch_recv_mr` / `dispatch_yield_mr` (FL4); `fl4HandleSyscall_recv` + `mtk_withoutPreemption` (spec);
  `jDispMR_of : NativeSys n c → JDispMRI → JDispMR`. **`JDispMRI`** [W] = `JDispMR` asked only for `InvSys` (Send / NBSend /
  Call) and `MidSys` (ReplyRecv / NBSendRecv / NBSendWait) numbers. Recv / NBRecv / Wait / NBWait / Yield: discharged.

## g5a (branch par/g5a in FL4-rb, on 607bd090 = int/j2 incl. g4a) — JEntryAtR3's seven joint premises: five DONE without a `JExt` field (`fnz`, `utks` theorems of `JAtZ`; `handlers`, `ports`, `urz` spec-only, asked once at the entry); `flags`, `vsTyp` NOT done (sizing below); P1 `hFr` DONE (spec-only `SpecFrPg` + `JAtZ.fpuFrameJ`); P7 `hno` NOT done (sizing below); top `kernel_entryJ35E`
Goal (brief): the seven `JEntryAtR3` joint fields (flags, handlers, ports, vsTyp, fnz, urz, utks) as `JExt` fields with keep lemmas
at every producer, then `kernel_entryJ35E` whose `hK` no longer asks them. Before adding fields I checked each against what `JAtZ`
already carries and against INV-PLAN §2's spec-only / joint split; five need no field.

### (1) What each of the seven became
| field | before | now | how |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fnz` (FrNZ) | [J] at σb | theorem `JAtZ.fnzJ` | `fcap` (every non-device frame cap's bytes in `UFr σ`) at byte 0 gives a spec data page at 0 (`0 &&& ~~~mask = 0`), hence `H ⟨0⟩ = other n` (`SpecCover.arch`), contradicting `JKern.h0` |
| `utks` (UtNodesJ) | [J] at σb | theorem `JAtZ.utksJ` (`utNodesJ_of_ks`) | **cone edit**: `UtKsApart`'s third part (ScPlaceUt) strengthened from "misses the ASID table `[ksb+288000, +16384)`" to "misses `[ksb+13568, ksb+304384)`" (all 64 nodes and the ASID table; with part one, the whole static area after the kernel-state base). Carried exactly as before: `UtKsApart.keep` copies it, the retype's children (`JCovD.retypeS`) get it by the same `omega` from the source's; `UtKsApart.asidOf` gives the old shape where a consumer needs it (UtResetTopJ). True in reachable states: the static kernel-state block (ks + `MAX_NODES` = 64 nodes + ASID table) is kernel-image data, never in a RAM untyped (l4v `valid_global_refs` / `kernel_window`; the same justification `UtNodesJ`'s docstring gave) |
| `handlers` (HandlersActive) | [J] joint at σb | [J] spec `SpecIrqH σ` at the entry | `JAtZ.handlersJ` = IntInv's `handlersActive_of_spec` with `StateRel`, `MdbLinks` (`xtop.rel`) and `IrqRel` (`xtop.fin`) |
| `ports` (IoPortsAlloc) | [J] joint at σb | [J] spec `SpecIoP σ` at the entry | `JAtZ.portsJ` = `ioPortsAlloc_of_spec` with `IoRel` |
| `urz` (UtZero) | [J] joint at σb | [J] spec `SpecUtZ σ` at the entry | `JAtZ.urzJ`: an MDB slot's RAM untyped cap is the spec's `untypedCap false p sb fi` there (`StateRel.abs_cap`, `absCap`) |
| `flags` (FlagsRel) | [J] joint | unchanged [J] joint | (3) |
| `vsTyp` (OffTabOK) | [J] joint | unchanged [J] joint | (3) |
| P1 `hFr` (`JThreadPath`, FpuFrameJHyp) | [J] joint at σb, at `extra[0]` | [J] spec `SpecFrPg σ` at the entry | `JAtZ.fpuFrameJ` (1b) |

Why spec-only and not `JExt` for handlers / ports / urz: at a `JAtZ` state each is equivalent (through `StateRel` / `IrqRel` /
`IoRel`, which every `JAtZ` carries) to a predicate on the spec state alone — l4v's `valid_irq_handlers`, `valid_ioports`,
`untyped_ranges_zero`, which l4v carries on the abstract side. As `JExt` fields every one of the ~80 `JAtZ` producers would
re-prove a spec fact through FL4 footprints (the IRQ-state words, the IO bitmap, every spec memory store); on the spec side the
keep lemma is one spec-only theorem per field over the syscall (INV-PLAN §4 G1 shape, off the cone).

New spec-only module **SpecInvG5** (namespace `SInvR.G5`; imports SpecInvUtR / SpecInvVfhR only): `SpecIrqH`, `SpecIoP`,
`SpecUtZ`, `SpecFrPg` (on `SInvU.capAt`, l4v `caps_of_state`), the bundle `SInvI`, `SInvI.frame` (caps, interrupt states,
allocated IO ports, memory and arch objects kept), `capAt_updTcb` (a TCB replaced by one with the same caps), `archObj_updTcb`.

### (1b) P1 `hFr` (the Thread path's `JThreadPath`, ReadFPU's destination frame)
- `FpuFrameJHyp Z s σ x` (XTopJointReadFpu) is now asked only when `x` is a slot of the typed heap
  (`∀ sl0, AbsSlot Z.th sl0 → x = cslotAddr sl0 → …`). Before, `JThreadPath.hFr` asked it at `extra[0]` whatever that was; with
  no extra cap the array pads with slot 0 (`NO_EXTRA_CAPS`), so the old premise constrained the word at address 0, which nothing
  else does (observation, not a finding: no trace that the word decodes to a RAM frame cap; the guard removes the question).
  The one consumer `tcb_read_fpuJ` already had the slot (`XcRel` gives `x0 = cslotAddr sl0`, `AbsSlot`); one-line change. Cone
  edit: everything downstream of XTopJointReadFpu rebuilt.
- New spec-only invariant `SpecFrPg σ` (fourth field `SInvI.frP`): every non-device spec `pageCap` lies in one non-device spec
  data page (l4v `valid_cap` of a `PageCap`, `typ_at (AArch (AUserData sz)) p`, weakened to "inside" for FL4's DeriveSubframe
  aliases, which are 4 KiB caps inside a 2 MiB page). Carried to σb by `sinvI_disp` (the FaultIP write replaces only the current
  TCB: `archObj_updTcb`).
- `JAtZ.fpuFrameJ J hS x : FpuFrameJHyp Z s σ x` (`StateRel.abs_cap` at the slot: the spec's cap is `absCap` of the FL4 frame

## g4c (branch par/g4c in FL4-q, on 607bd090, rebased onto int/j2 857ac23e) — g4a (6) (G-a): spec `kentry_nofail` under `SInvX`. STOPPED on a FINDING: `SInvX` is too weak for no-fail (it has no `valid_objs` typing of cap / TCB / queue references and no `valid_ep` shape), so `kentry_nofail` is false as a statement over `SInvX` states; no Lean change, no new top (`kernel_entryJ36` / `kernel_entry_reachN` NOT stated)
Documentation only (this section). No proof file edited, nothing built (nothing to build); `g4c.sh` (= rd14hs.sh, renamed logs) untracked.

### (1) What was asked and why it fails
- Target: `kentry_nofail : SInvX σ → σ.curThread ≠ σ.idleThread → numDomains = 1 → ¬ (fl4KernelEntrySyscall true c σ).2` for every
  native `c`, then drop `KPostX`'s left disjunct. `NonDet` failure (`Fl4Spec/Monad.lean`) is the Prop `.2`: `fail`, `assert P` with `¬P`,
  `assertOpt none`, `getsThe` of `none`, `stateAssert`, a `whileLoop` with a failing reachable round **or an infinite run**, and
  `lfp` (rec_del / cap_revoke) failing at every pre-fixed point. `bind` fails if any reachable continuation fails, so no-fail needs a
  wp-style precondition at every intermediate state (l4v: `no_fail` + `valid` under `invs`).
- l4v discharges the abstract entry's asserts with `invs`: mainly `valid_objs` (every cap's / TCB field's / queue's reference names
  an object of the right type: `valid_cap`, `valid_tcb`, `valid_ep`, `valid_ntfn`, `valid_reply`, `valid_sched_context`), `sym_refs`,
  `valid_sched` and the refill invariants, plus termination of the loops. **`SInvX` carries only slices of these.** In particular
  it has no field saying that an endpoint cap names an endpoint:
  - `CnDom` (SInvA.cnDom) types CNode caps only (`CnOk`: `cnodeCap p r g → CnFull σ p r`);
  - `UtInv3` (SInvA.ut): `CapKindV` types *slot-holding* caps relative to each other (`shp c = shp c'`), `UtChV` / `CapFreeV` / `UtFreeV`
    speak about caps inside untyped regions; none says that the object at a non-slot cap's reference exists or has its type;
  - `ScKindR` (SInvA.sl.2) types SC caps relative to each other; `SpecGlobS` / `IdleOutV` only exclude the IRQ nodes / the idle thread
    as references; `EpQB` / `NtfnQB` (SInvA.epq / .nq) type the *members* of queues of existing endpoints / notifications.
- **Counter-scenario** (an `SInvX` state, not a reachable one): any `SInvX` state with `ct ≠ idle` in which some slot of ct's CSpace
  that ct can name holds `endpointCap p b rights` with `AllowSend ∈ rights`, `p` outside every untyped region, not an IRQ node,
  not the idle thread, and `σ.kheap p = none` (or a notification). Every `SInvX` field quantifying over caps is satisfied by such a cap
  (CnDom: not a CNode cap; CapKind / CnShape / IfUnsafe: not slot-holding, not in an untyped region; UtCh / CapFree / UtFree /
  UtDesc: outside every untyped; ScKindR: not an SC cap and `p` in no SC cap's range; SpecGlobS / IdleOutV: `p` excluded; NativeScopeS:
  not a VT-x cap; ValidIrqHandlers: not an IRQ handler cap; IfLiveT / ScLiveT: extra caps only add holders; the scheduler, refill,
  queue and SC-binding fields do not read slots). `sysSend` / `sysNBSend` / `sysCall` with the cap register naming that slot:
  `fl4HandleInvocationR` → `fl4DecodeInvocation` (`Ext/Invocation.lean:163`, returns `invokeEndpoint p …`) → `performInvocation`
  (`Syscall.lean:82`) → `sendIpc` → `getEndpoint p` → `getSimpleKo` → `getObject p` = `getsThe none` (KHeap.lean:87) → **fails**.
  So `kentry_nofail` does not follow from `SInvX`. This is NOT a kernel / spec mismatch: at a `JReach` state the `JAtZ` relation ties the
  spec cap to an FL4 endpoint object, and l4v's `valid_objs` holds there; the bundle just lacks the fact. (A formal counterexample would
  need a concrete `SInvX` state with `ct ≠ idle`; none exists in the repo: `boot_sinvX` is at `initASt`, where ct = idle. Not built.)
- A second independent gap of the same kind: `sendIpc`'s `.recvEP [] => fail` (Ipc.lean:231) and `receiveIpc`'s `assert (q ≠ [])`
  (Ipc.lean:315) need l4v `valid_ep`'s "a non-idle endpoint has a non-empty queue"; `EpQB` does not give it (`.recvEP []` satisfies
  `EpQB` vacuously). Likewise the receiver-state match (`| _ => fail`, Ipc.lean:214) needs "every member of a recvEP queue is
  BlockedOnReceive" (EpQB gives only `epBlocked y.tcbState = some e`, i.e. send *or* receive).

### (1) `SInvI`'s four fields
| field | g5a | now | how |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SpecIrqH` (handler caps: `irq ≤ maxIRQ` ∧ not inactive) | [J] spec at the entry | **gone** | the bound was never used: `handlersActive_of_spec` re-derived `i < 128` from it, but FL4's `CapValid` of the handler cap (`hca.1`) already gives `i < 128`. Without the bound it is l4v `valid_irq_handlers`, carried in `SInvX` since vih3 (`SInvA.vih`, `kentry_validIrqMasks` / `vi_fl4CallKernel`). `handlersActive_of_vih`, `JAtZ.handlersJV`; at σb by `vih_disp` (FaultIP keeps every cap, `update_time_stamp` the interrupt states) |
| `SpecFrPg` (a non-device page cap inside one spec data page) | [J] spec at the entry | **gone** | `FpuFrameJHyp` restated per byte: every byte of the slot's frame cap is in a spec user frame (`UFr`). That is `JAtZ.fcap` at the slot, so `JAtZ.fpuFrameJ J x` needs no spec fact. The consumer `JAtZ.copyFrameJ` needs only one data page per written word (`ufr_word`: an 8-aligned `UFr` word's page, `inUserFrame`'s base, holds all 8 bytes); `tcb_read_fpuJ` carries the per-byte fact across the caller's restart (`UFr.keep`) |
| `SpecIoP` (l4v `valid_ioports`) | [J] spec at the entry | unchanged, in **`SInvIR`** | not carried over a syscall (3) |
| `SpecUtZ` (l4v `untyped_ranges_zero`) | [J] spec at the entry | unchanged, in **`SInvIR`** | not carried over a syscall (3) |

- **`JReachI`**: `start` from `JAtZ ∧ SInvX ∧ SInvIR ∧ MR`; `step` along `RJM` (J36E's exit relation) **and `SInvIR` of the exit** (the

### (3) Not done, with sizing
- **`kentry_sinvIR` / `kcall_sinvIR`** (`SpecIoP`, `SpecUtZ` across every syscall and event): not started in Lean; both are true in
  reachable states (no FINDING), but neither is a frame of an existing kit:

    an extra field **`IoNoOverlap`** (l4v `ioports_no_overlap`: two IO-port caps with overlapping ranges have equal ranges) — without it

    exactly the part the new free index exposes, chunk order top-down), retype (free index only grows) and untyped cap copies (same free
    part). Size: L (a new memory frame family over the whole call graph plus the range field's own carry through retype / detype).

## m61 (branch par/m61 in FL4-m56, on 53035417 = par/m60) — (d) in part: m60's read bundle was false in reachable states in three places (fixed, 377b8584); the general fault path's m58 reads (`FaultReads`) DERIVED from entry-state facts (`FaultEnt`), with the run's footprint and keep-lemmas to the meeting state and the inversion of `schedulable_here`; m59's `UsOff` DERIVED (`usOff_of`, from the SC placement at the entry state); `FinReads`, `FaultEnt` from `EntryInv`, `entry_of6`, ReplyRecv R1–R7, `kernel_entryJ33F` / `J34F` NOT done; no kernel FINDING
- **Proof-side finding (m60's bundle, not fastpath.rs): `FastFaultOK` (hence `entry_of5`'s `hFt`) was false in every
  reachable state where `fastpath.fault` accepts.** Three of its read conditions asked more than the general path reads:
  (i) `TabOff` quantified over every `hi` / `lo : U64`; `atAF ksb hi` / `peAF p lo` then range over every word congruent to
  `ksb` / `p` mod 8, so `TabOff s A` (and `VmOff`, `FinCommon.hvn`) was false for every aligned `A`. Fixed: `hi < 2048`,
  `lo < 512` (what `find_asid` reads: `hi &&& 2047`, `asid &&& 511`; `and2047_lt`, `and511_lt`), as P3 `VsRel.table` /
  `pool` already state it. (ii) `FinCommon.htm` / `hrl` asked TIMER_MIN = 0 and RELEASE_HEAD = 0; `schedulable_here`
  accepts with a timeout pending but not due and with a release queue whose head is not ready. Replaced by **`NoDue`** (the
  disjunctions `awaken_none` / `schedule_cn` take) at the enqueued state, inside each `FinReads` case (`∀ v1 v2` for the
  empty-queue case's bitmap words). (iii) `UsOff.wf` asked `RefillsWF` of the handler's SC whenever it is nonzero; a bound
  SC that was never configured (`REFILL_MAX = 0`) passes `schedulable_here` (it checks `sc ≠ 0` only), and its refills

## g4e (branch par/g4e in FL4-q, on d4d7d09b = int/j2 incl. g4b, g5a, g4c) — g4c's handoff (`fl4CallKernel` for the other events): inventory of the non-syscall entries; `JReachE` / `jreach_invE` / `kernel_entry_reachE` with syscall AND event steps; the combined syscall top `kernel_entryJ37N` (g4c's no-fail post with g4b's `MR` carry)
New leaf only (XTopJointKEntryEv; root import after XTopJointKEntryNF). Nothing existing edited.

### (1) Inventory: joint refinement of the non-syscall FL4 entries (before proving)
FL4's entries (crates/fl4-core/src/syscall.rs, arch/x86_64/syscall.rs; called from fl4-kernel/src/entry.rs) and the spec event of
`fl4CallKernel` each one corresponds to:
| FL4 entry | body | spec event | joint top at the entry | joint pieces that exist (and what they assume) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `handle_interrupt_entry s a irq` | `update_timestamp; check_budget; handle_interrupt irq; finish` | `.interrupt` (`updateTimeStamp; checkBudget; maybeHandleInterrupt`) | **none** (no theorem mentions `syscall.handle_interrupt_entry` in P3; only P1 queue lemmas and ScEntry's Sched-level `entry_check_budget_refines` at `SchedRel`/`Inv`, not JAtZ) | `JAtZ.handleIrqJIN` (XTopJointIrqZI: `handle_interrupt` at `JAtZ`, post "line inactive ∨ JAt after"; premises `IrqPlat` [P], `NativeScope σ`, the line number `w = i`, `w ≠ 126, 127`); `check_budget` at J only inside the preemption path (`JHole.afterInvJZI` etc., XTopJointPreempt*); `jat_finishJRNM` (finish from `JAtZR` with `MR`). Missing: `update_timestamp; check_budget` at a `JAtZ` entry state ending in `JAtZ`/`JAtZR`, the FL4 `irq` argument vs the spec's `getActiveIRQ` (a [P] fact on `MR`'s oracle position), the composition |
| `handle_user_exception s a number code` | `if budget_ok then handle_fault ct (UserException number code); finish` | `.userLevelFault w1 w2` (`withoutPreemption`: `updateTimeStamp; checkBudgetRestart; when … handleFault ct (userException …)`) | **none** | `JAtZ.budgetOkB` (syscall front's budget check, used by `kernel_entryJ13PUG*`); `handle_fault` at J only for cap faults (`JAtZ.faultHypJZ{C,N,M}`, `CapFaultCorr f f'`, at mid states `MidC/MidN/MidE` with `schedulerAction ≠ resume`); no `UserException` message correspondence at J; `jat_finishJRNM` |
| `handle_vm_fault s a addr code` | `if budget_ok then handle_fault ct (vm_fault addr code instr); finish` | `.vmFaultEvent ft` (`handleVmFault` reads the fault address from the machine, then `handleFault`) | **none** | as the user exception; the spec's `getFaultAddr` vs FL4's `addr` is a [P] machine fact |
| `handle_syscall s a n`, `n` outside `[SYSCALL_MIN, SYSCALL_MAX]` or `TRAP_SYSCALLS` set | `FAULT_IP` write, then `handle_unknown_syscall` (debug / TLS / `SysVMEnter` arms, else `unknown_syscall_fault`) | FaultIP write, then `.unknownSyscall m` | **none** (`kernel_entryJ*` take `hn : NativeSys n c` and `hflag`) | the FaultIP write at J (`JAtZ.regWrJ`, inside `kernel_entryJ13PUG*`); `budget_ok` at J; no unknown-syscall fault at J |
| `handle_trap_syscall s a vector` (x86 `int $N`) | `FAULT_IP` write, then the unknown syscall (or #GP user exception under `TRAP_SYSCALLS`) | FaultIP write, then `.unknownSyscall m` or `.userLevelFault 13 _` | **none** | as above |
| `handle_debug_exception` | debug API | no spec event | — | [S]: the hardware debug API is not in the spec |
| `handle_vcpu_exit` | VT-x | `.hypervisorEvent` | — | [S] VT-x out of scope |
So no non-syscall event has a joint refinement theorem; every one becomes the per-step premise `JEvRef` below (no KPostXS-style
post was available to reuse).

### (2) The pieces (XTopJointKEntryEv)
- **`KPostMS` / `KPostXMS`**: `KPostM` / `KPostXM` without the spec-fails disjunct (∃ σ' outcome, `RJ`, `MR`, and `SInvX σ'`).
  `KPostMS.toM`, `KPostXMS.toXM`, `KPostXMS.toXS` (to g4c's `KPostXS`).
- **`kPreFinAtGMS`, `kernel_entryJ13PUGMS`**: g4b's `kPreFinAtGM` / `kernel_entryJ13PUGM` with the post `KPostMS` (same bodies; the
  fail disjunct came only from `kPreFinAtGM`'s left disjunct, never produced — g4c's observation for `kernel_entryJ13PUG`).
- **`kernel_entryJ37N`**: `kernel_entryJ37`'s premises exactly (incl. `hDM : JDispMRI` [W]); `hFast` [P] now at `KPostMS`
  (m57's `FastRR` shape, the post changed as g4c did); post **`KPostXMS`**: an outcome σ' of `fl4KernelEntrySyscall true c σ` with
  `RJ`, `MR r.2 σ'.ms` and `SInvX σ'`. No spec-fails disjunct, no `MR →`.
- Events: **`KEv`** (`irq w | user number code | vmf addr code | sysU n | trap vector`), `KEv.run` (the FL4 function of each),
  **`KEvSpec e fip ev`** (the spec event, `fip = true` for `sysU` / `trap`: the FaultIP write comes first; `KEvSpec.not_sys`),
  **`EvOut fip ev σ σ'`** (σ' an outcome of `fl4CallKernel true ev` at σ, or at a FaultIP outcome of σ when `fip`),
  `sinvX_evOut` (`SInvX` at every `EvOut` outcome: `kcall_sinvX`, across the FaultIP write by `SInvXFip`, with `cfk_fip` for
  ct / idle).
- **`JEvRef e fip ev s a σ`** [W] (the named per-step premise of an event, at that event's entry state): `e.run st arI s a ⦃ r =>
  ∃ σ', EvOut fip ev σ σ' ∧ RJM r.1 r.2 σ' ⦄` (KPostXS-style: returns, related, `MR`, no spec-fails disjunct). Its [P] part is the
  argument agreement (pending line, fault address / kind with the spec's machine reads).
- **`SInvXFip σ`** [W] (only for the two `fip` entries, at their entry state): `∀ w ∈ (fl4SyscallFaultIP σ.curThread σ).1, SInvX
  w.2`. `kentry_sinvX` carries the FaultIP prefix only inside the syscall proof (rd8w's `kentry_rdyOffW` with per-field `*_fip`
  lemmas), not as a standalone `SInvW` lemma; a standalone `sinvW_fip` (every SInvW field across one register write of ct) would
  discharge it (spec-only, S–M: the `*_fip` / `IK` kits exist per field).

### (3) The induction
- **`JReachE arI AR MR`**: `start` (any `JAtZ` at some ghosts ∧ `SInvX` ∧ `MR`), `step n c` (as `JReachM.step`: native syscall,
  ct ≠ idle [S], `handle_syscall = ok (s', a')`, σ' ∈ the spec entry, `RJM`), `event e fip ev` (`KEvSpec e fip ev`, `ev ≠ .interrupt
  → ct ≠ idle` [S], `fip = true → SInvXFip σ` [W], `e.run = ok (s', a')`, `EvOut fip ev σ σ'`, `RJM s' a' σ'`). `JReachM.toE`.
- **`jreach_invE (hnd)`**: `JReachE s a σ → (∃ ghosts, JAtZ) ∧ SInvX σ ∧ MR a σ.ms` (`kentry_sinvX`, `sinvX_evOut`).
- **`kernel_entry_reachE`** (the [P] bundle of J37, `hRef`, `hPI`, `hnd`): `JReachE s a σ → ∃ ghosts, JAtZ ∧ SInvX ∧ MR ∧`
  (i) `∀ n c, ct ≠ idle → NativeSys n c → hflag → hK → hDM (JDispMRI) → hFin → hFast (KPostMS) → handle_syscall ⦃ r => ∃ σ' ∈
  entry, RJ ∧ SInvX σ' ∧ MR ∧ JReachE r.1 r.2 σ' ⦄` and (ii) `∀ e fip ev, KEvSpec e fip ev → (ev ≠ interrupt → ct ≠ idle) → (fip →
  SInvXFip σ) → JEvRef e fip ev s a σ → e.run ⦃ r => ∃ σ', EvOut fip ev σ σ' ∧ RJ ∧ SInvX σ' ∧ MR ∧ JReachE r.1 r.2 σ' ⦄`.
  One induction for `JAtZ ∧ SInvX ∧ MR`, no spec-fails case, no `MR` premise in any step.

### (4) Remaining premises (exactly)
- Syscall steps: as g4b (4) minus (G-a): the [P] platform (`PlainStore`, `hARI hA hM hKD hPA hIA hmrt hmb hT hmax htu`, `hRef`,
  `hPI`, `hFast` now for `KPostMS`, the [P] fields of hK / hFin), the [S] scope (ct ≠ idle, `NativeSys`, `hflag`, `numDomains = 1`,
  the VT-x cases of hK), the (d) bundles hK (E4–E10, P1, P7, P9, P10, Untyped / device [J]) and hFin (F1, F6) at the reachable
  state's ghosts, and `hDM : JDispMRI` [W] at the dispatch states.
- Event steps: **`JEvRef`** [W] per event at its entry state (five FL4 entries, (1)); **`SInvXFip`** [W] for `sysU` / `trap` at the
  entry state; the [S] `ev ≠ interrupt → ct ≠ idle`. Out of the induction ([S]): `handle_debug_exception`, `handle_vcpu_exit`.

### (5) Findings
None. Checked: `JEvRef` is asked per FL4 entry and argument at one state (never ∀ states), and is l4v-shaped (the corres of
`handle_event`/`call_kernel` per event); its instance for arguments that disagree with the spec's machine reads (a line that is
not pending, a wrong fault address) is false, but such an instance is never assumed by any step: it is the hypothesis of a
conditional clause of `kernel_entry_reachE` and of nothing else. `SInvXFip` is expected true at every `SInvX` state (only ct's FaultIP register changes; not proved here,
the syscall carry `kentry_sinvX` already passes the same write) — not a finding, a missing standalone lemma.

### (6) Builds and axioms
- tokyo, FL4-q mirror (./g4e.sh untracked = g4c.sh with its own log name; scratch/g4e/ax.lean untracked). The mirror's cache was
  warm (1691 oleans) but from g4c's tree, so g4e-b1 rebuilt the cone touched by the int/j2 merges (~300 modules) and then the new
  module: "Build completed successfully (6914 jobs)", first try, no sorry / admit / native_decide / bv_decide. **g4e-full1** (full `lake build Fl4Proofs` at 370adcb4): "Build completed successfully (6989 jobs)", 0 `declaration uses sorry`.
- Axioms (g4e-b1, repeated after g4e-full1 with the same result): kernel_entryJ37N, kernel_entryJ13PUGMS, kPreFinAtGMS, jreach_invE, kernel_entry_reachE, JReachM.toE,
  sinvX_evOut, KPostXMS.toXS: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; KEvSpec.not_sys: none.

### (7) Next (handoff)
- `JEvRef` for the interrupt entry first (most pieces exist): `update_timestamp; check_budget` at a `JAtZ` entry state (the
  preemption path's J-level `check_budget` proofs, lifted from `JHole` to `JAtZ`), `JAtZ.handleIrqJIN` (its inactive-line disjunct
  closed by `SInvX`'s `ValidIrqMasks` with the pending line), `jat_finishJRNM`, and a [P] fact that the hardware `irq` is the line
  the spec's `getActiveIRQ` returns at `MR`'s oracle position.
- `JEvRef` for user exceptions / VM faults: `budget_ok` at J exists (`JAtZ.budgetOkB`); needs `handle_fault` at a budget-checked
  entry state for `UserException` / `VMFault` messages (today only `CapFaultCorr` at mid states).
- `SInvXFip`: a standalone `sinvX_fip : SInvX σ → ∀ w ∈ fl4SyscallFaultIP σ.curThread σ, SInvX w.2` (spec-only).
- Still open from g4b / g4a: `JDispMRI`, the (d) bundles of hK / hFin.

## g4f (branch par/g4f in FL4-q, on 3f144df1 = int/j2 incl. g4e) — g4e's handoff: (1) `sinvX_fip` DONE (`SInvXFip` discharged); (2) `JEvRef` for the interrupt entry DONE from a non-idle thread (one [P] hardware fact `IrqHw`, MR across `handle_interrupt` proved); (3) user-exception / VM-fault entries: budget check and finish DONE, the fault branch stays one narrowed [W] `JFltHyp`; unknown-syscall / `int $N` NOT done; (4) `JReachE2` / `jreach_invE2` / `kernel_entry_reachE2` DONE
New leaves only: SpecInvG4f (spec side), XTopJointKEntryEv2 (root imports after XTopJointKEntryEv). Nothing existing edited.

### (1) `SInvX` across the FaultIP write (SpecInvG4f)
- **`sinvWR_fip`**: `SInvW σ ∧ RPos σ → ∀ w ∈ (fl4SyscallFaultIP t σ).1, SInvW w.2 ∧ RPos w.2` for any `t`. Every one of the
  ~40 fields from its family's `fl4SyscallFaultIP` kit: the cap view `uV` (`uk_`: `IdleOutV`, `UtInv3`, `ScKindR`,
  `IdleScOutV`, `SpecGlobS` / `HasTC` through `capAt = uV.2.1`), the IRQ node (`nk_`), the idle pair (`fld_arch`), the binding
  frame `BR` (`sb_` + `scInv_of_br`), `vfc_auto` (`VfhAll ∧ CnDom`), `b_of_gf` + `fg_` (`FaultTcbsS ∧ NQB`), the `IK` leaves
  (`ns_ dl_ hv_ gk_ nq_ il_ vi_ oi_ sl_ nb_ tq_ sa_ q4_ rb_ ba_ ve_ rd_ pz_`, P19's `ctExit/ctQ/simple/curScT`), and three by
  `ik_arch_fip` (`RS`, `OffReady`, `CAx`: they read no `tcbArch`).
- **`sinvX_fip : SInvX σ → SInvXFip σ`** (XTopJointKEntryEv2). `SInvXFip` [W] is gone from every statement below.

### (2) The interrupt entry (XTopJointKEntryEv2)
- **`JAtZ.utCheckB`**: FL4's `update_timestamp; check_budget` at an `Entered` `JAtZ` state under `KBudgetB`, every outcome:
  an outcome z of the spec's `updateTimeStamp; checkBudget` with the same flag and `JAtZ` at z (budgetOkB's cases without the
  restart: `timestampJ` + `check_budgetT` for a sufficient head, `timestampJH` + the hole's `checkBudgetF` / `checkBudgetT` /
  `checkBudgetTR` for the charge, every timeout-handler endpoint state).
- **`JAtZ.handleIrqJIM`**: MRPath's `handleIrqJIAN` with `MR a σ.ms` in and `MR r.2 z.2.ms` at the chosen outcome (FL4's
  masks are the spec's by `MachPlat.mask`, `w.bv.setWidth 8 = i`; acks by `MachPlat.ack`; `send_signal` by MachKeep's
  `MK.notification_send_signal`, the spec's `sendSignal` keeping `msF`). Needs `w < 256`. (Also usable for the preemption
  path's MR carry, which today sits inside g4b's `JDispMR` [W].)
- **`IrqHw AR MR a a' σ w`** [P] (the one new premise, asked at the entry state of the step): the line `w` the hardware took is
  the spec's `gaiLine false σ.ms` line, `w < 256`, `w ≠ 126, 127` (FL4's IPI vectors, one core [S]), `MR a' (gaiState σ.ms)`
  for the arch state `a'` the entry runs at (the IRQ oracle advanced once, as `MachPlat.take` does), `AR a c → AR a' c`.
- **`jEvRef_irq`**: from `JAtZ` at (s,a,σ), `SInvX σ`, `ct ≠ idle`, `IrqHw a a' σ w`, the syscall top's [P] bundle and
  `hFin` (`KFinAtR31` at the pre-finish states of this run, FL4 states pinned by `KFrontI`, as the syscall top's `hFin`):
  `handle_interrupt_entry s a' w ⦃ ∃ σ', EvOut false .interrupt σ σ' ∧ RJ ∧ MR ⦄`. The clock read by `nowAgree_gai`, MR across
  `update_timestamp; check_budget` (`ut_cb_mr`) and the spec's (`mfk_checkBudget`), the spec's IRQ read at the budget-checked
  state reports `i` (`gaiLine_congr`, masks / IRQ position kept), the inactive-line case refuted by `ValidIrqMasks`
  (`msF_vim`, `gaiLine_unmasked`), `NativeScope` / `FpuOwnOK` at the pre-finish state by `ns_handleEvent` /
  `fo_handleEvent_int`, then `jat_finishJRNM`.

### (3) Fault entries
- **`jEvRef_flt`** (generic): an entry `budget_ok; if b then B; finish` whose spec event is

- **`JFltHyp AR MR Z H Cs B G s a σ`** [W]: at every budget-checked state of this run (`budget_ok s a = ok (true, s1, a1)`,
  the spec's check at σb, `JAtZ` at the entry ghosts Z H Cs, `MR`), `B s1 a1 ⦃ ∃ z ∈ G σb, JAtZR ∧ MR ⦄`. l4v:

- **`JReachE2`**: `start`, `step` (as `JReachE`), **`irq w`** (`IrqHw a a1 σ w`, `handle_interrupt_entry s a1 w = ok`,

### (5) Remaining premises (exactly)
- Syscall steps: unchanged from g4e (4).
- Interrupt from a non-idle thread: `IrqHw` [P] (entry state), `KFinEv .interrupt` = `KFinAtR31` (F1 hd, F3/F4 arch,
  F6 sni, F7 send, F8 tail) at the pre-finish states, the [P] bundle (`ARIface`, `ArchTotal`, `numDomains = 1`,

  SC and `CurInv` there are not covered by `utCheckB`, which needs `Entered`). `SInvXFip`: none.

### (6) Reachability check of the new premises
- `IrqHw`: for the model platform (arch state = machine state, MachRel's `modelArch`) the hardware's take is
  `a' = gaiState σ.ms`, the line is the oracle's, `w = i.toNat < 256`; it fails only for a line 126 / 127 (an IPI vector:
  single core [S]) or a masked / 0xFF oracle value (no interrupt delivered: no step). Asked at one state, in a conditional
  clause; not a statement over all states.
- `JFltHyp`: l4v-shaped and expected true in reachable runs given the hardware argument ranges: FL4 sends `number`/`code`
  (resp. `fsr`) unmasked where the spec masks to 32/28 (resp. 5) bits; x86 vectors are < 32 and exception / page-fault
  error codes fit those masks with PKE / CET off. A run with a wider error code would make the premise (of that clause)
  false, never assumed elsewhere.
- `KFinEv`: the same bundle the syscall top asks at its pre-finish states (g4a (d)).
